newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares rally, end firm on economic news.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares rally, end firm on economic news.

text.p: Chilean blue chips rallied to close nearly one percent higher as a welter of economic figures pointed to a faster-than-expected slowdown in the economy, giving rise to hopes interest rates could fall.
The government's Imacec index showed growth cooling to 5.8 percent in July from 7.5 percent in the same month last year.
"The Imacec index for July was lower than expectations, which is good news for interest rate watchers," said Lance Eckel, an analyst at brokerage Sud Americano.
The selective IPSA index ended up 0.94 percent at 99.14 points. The IGPA index firmed 0.48 percent at 5,454.24 points.
Trade was moderate with volume of 8.3 billion pesos.
The light turnover may mean the rally could be short lived with the momentum petering out in coming sessions, said analysts.
"The market should show some strength, but not to any great extent," said David Hurd, head of research at Merrill Lynch.
Investors will be paying close attention to the Federal Reserve's policy meeting on Tuesday for any change in U.S interest rates, said dealers.

Traders said the market shrugged off foreign trade figures showing the trade deficit widening to $267 million in August -- the largest monthly deficit since 1990 -- mainly as the result of a sharp fall in copper prices.
"People weren't surprised by the figures. The fact is commodity prices are falling and the peso is strong, which is bound to push imports higher," said one trader.
Copper accounts for some 40 percent of Chile's exports.
Analysts were divided as to when the Central Bank would ease its tight-credit policy imposed late last year to cool the economy, which had been in danger of overheating.
Some said it could be towards the end of the year, while others said the bank would wait until the first quarter of 1997 to be certain that all indicators pointed to a slowdown in growth.
"What is clear is the Imacec figure gives the bank more room to manoeuvre earlier than anticipated," said one dealer.
Gainers included steel company Cap, up 3.13 percent at 1,320 pesos, power utility Endesa, up 1.75 percent at 262 pesos and drug company LabChile which rose 1.52 percent to 335 pesos.
Losers included power utility Edelnor, down 2.78 percent at 350 pesos and copper products maker Madeco which shed 1.06 percent to 935 pesos.
